doc.title: Annie Ross interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 13, 2001

title: Favorite moments and jazz as feeling beyond color
summary: Her heart is in singing; she says jazz is feeling, not about color, though it is a black music.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Looking back: no regrets, what it all meant

blocks.x: If you look back on the time since there, is there a favorite thing that you were doing? The theater? Would that have been the —

No. My heart is singing, and will always be. But there were wonderful moments in each of the things that I did. You know the opening night of “Three Penny Opera” in London was phenomenal. But, then there’s “Sing a Song of Basie.” No, and all this analytical stuff about jazz—
What do you think about that?

Not a lot. Jazz is feeling. It’s feeling. It has nothing to do with color. You know we know that it is a black music. But you can’t dismiss a lot of people. It’s not about that, it’s about love and giving and joy and enrichment. I never had a problem with that.
I hope that statement goes in your book.
You call me, I’ll help you out.
